overview: The Mina Cho Quartet performed a set at the 2026 Medford Jazz Festival, showcasing 'gugak jazz' which fuses Korean traditional rhythms and melodies with modern jazz improvisation. The performance featured original compositions and interpretations of Korean folk music.

items.title: Introduction of the Mina Cho Quartet
items.summary: Terry Carter introduced Dr. Mina Cho and her quartet, describing their musical style as a fusion of century-old Korean ritual traditions and modern jazz.

items.title: Performance: G Street Dance
items.summary: Mina Cho introduced the first piece, 'G Street Dance,' which is built upon the traditional Korean shamanic rhythm known as gukgeori jangdan.

items.title: Performance: Unmyeong (Destiny)
items.summary: The quartet performed 'Unmyeong,' a composition Cho described as exploring the themes of fate and the coincidences that bring people together.

items.title: Performance: Dalmaji (Greeting the Moon)
items.summary: Cho introduced 'Dalmaji,' also titled 'Night of the Full Moon,' a piece inspired by Asian traditions of celebrating the full moon to wish for a rich harvest.

items.title: Performance: Miryang Arirang
items.summary: The group performed an arrangement of 'Miryang Arirang,' a traditional folk melody from the northeastern region of Korea.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Festival Announcements
items.summary: Following a final encore, Terry Carter thanked the festival sponsors and announced the performance schedule for the following day.

subject: Mina Cho Quartet Performance
